info.name: movie-recommendation-system - Full Demo (via api-gateway)
info.description:
One narrative walk through every service, entirely through api-gateway (:8080) — the single front door for the whole system (ADR-0007). Run top-to-bottom; later requests reuse variables earlier ones set.

Story: register a user, browse/search the public catalog, prove the gateway actually enforces auth on the protected routes, check cold-start recommendations, write a review, then watch recommendations personalize once Kafka delivers the rating event to recommendation-service.

Each service also has its own deeper collection (CRUD, validation, error cases, direct-to-service ports) in that service's directory — this one is the single-pass demo, not a substitute for those.

Prerequisites: full docker-compose stack up (postgres, kafka, mongo, redis, catalog/search/review/recommendation/user-service, api-gateway) plus the standalone mflix-mongo container started (`docker start mflix-mongo`) so catalog/search-service have real seeded data.

Optional resilience check once you're through this collection: `docker kill` catalog-service or search-service mid-demo and re-run a browse/search request — api-gateway's circuit breaker returns a clean 503 fallback instead of hanging or a raw connection error (verified in ADR-0011 Update 4). Not automated here since it needs a manual docker command between requests.

variable.description: api-gateway - the only base URL this collection uses

item.name: 1. Register & Login
item.description: user-service, through the gateway. /api/users/register and /api/users/login are the only public user-service routes (see JwtAuthenticationGlobalFilter's allowlist).

item.name: 2. Browse & Search (public - no token needed)
item.description: catalog-service and search-service, through the gateway. /api/movies/** is on the public allowlist, so these work with no Authorization header at all - discovery is deliberately open.

exec: pm.test('response is a page of movies', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().content).to.be.an('array'); });
pm.test('response is a list of results', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('array'); });

item.name: 5. Semantic search (search-service, may 503 with no embedding key)

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 (embedding provider configured) or 503 (fails soft, no key set)', function () {
console.log('No EMBEDDING_PROVIDER API key configured for search-service - this 503 is expected fail-soft behavior, not a bug.');

url.raw: {{gatewayUrl}}/api/movies/search/vector?q=a hacker discovers reality is a simulation&limit=10

query.value: a hacker discovers reality is a simulation

item.name: 3. Prove the gateway enforces auth
item.description: /api/reviews/** and /api/recommendations/** are NOT on the public allowlist - a request with no Bearer token never reaches review-service/recommendation-service at all, api-gateway rejects it with 401 first.

item.name: 6. List reviews without a token returns 401
4. Cold-start recommendations (before any ratings)
item.description: This user has no ratings yet, so recommendation-service falls back to a global popularity list rather than erroring (see RecommendationServiceImpl.getRecommendations - cold start path).

item.name: 7. Recommendations for our new user (popularity fallback)
5. Seed content & write a review
item.description: Seed a fresh movie via catalog-service (public route), then rate it as our demo user through review-service (protected - needs the token).

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Demo Movie",
  "year": 2024,
  "plot": "Seeded by the full-demo Postman collection.",
  "genres": ["Sci-Fi", "Action"],
  "directors": ["Demo Director"],
  "cast": ["Demo Actor"],
  "countries": ["USA"],
  "languages": ["English"],
  "rated": "PG-13",
  "runtime": 120,
  "poster": "https://example.com/demo-movie.jpg"
}

item.name: 10. Rate it again - 409, a review already exists

exec: pm.test('error says already exists', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().errorMessage).to.include('already exists'); });

item.name: 6. Watch personalization kick in (Kafka async)
item.description: review-service published rating.updated/review.created to Kafka; recommendation-service's RatingEventConsumer picks it up asynchronously (typically 2-5s locally). Postman/Newman can't sleep mid-collection, so if this still looks like the cold-start baseline, just re-send this one request by hand after a few seconds.

item.name: 11. Recommendations after rating (may need a manual re-send)

exec: console.log('If this still matches the cold-start baseline from step 7, wait ~2-5s for Kafka delivery and re-send this request.');
pm.test('response is a list', function () { pm.expect(json).to.be.an('array'); });
